_doc: Story 4.2 GOLDEN FIXTURE — the VAT + quote-total policy pin (4.2-GOLDEN-01, R-403/R-404/R-410/R-411). Pins representative per-line VAT cases across the pilot Swedish VAT rates expressed as BASIS POINTS (0 / 600 / 1200 / 2500 bp = 0% / 6% / 12% / 25%). The VAT rate ALWAYS flows in from the fixture as a basis-point INPUT — the engine invents NO rate and holds NO percent constant, so there is NO hidden 0.25/25/1.25 literal in the VAT path (R-404, epic blocker). Per-line VAT = roundToOre(lineNetOre * vatRateBp / 10000) under the SINGLE Story 4.1 half-away-from-zero rounding mode (round PER LINE); section/quote VAT totals SUM the already-rounded per-line VAT values via sumOre (sum-of-rounded, NEVER round-of-sum, R-403). The `sumOfRoundedVsRoundOfSum` case is LOAD-BEARING: it pins the divergence where sum-of-rounded (3) != round-of-summed-VAT (2) so an accidental round-at-end fails loud. Each case carries an `origin` label — `new-expected` (the pilot's explicit VAT assumption) or `documented-delta` (an intentional divergence from Lovable's hardcoded-25% behaviour). Money/rate numbers ONLY — NO PII (personnummer/orgnr/name/email/address), NO clock (NFR17/R-411). This per-line VAT rounding policy + the excl/incl/both display policy + the 'private customer -> always incl-VAT' presentation invariant are CONSERVATIVE PILOT ASSUMPTIONS pending owner/accounting sign-off (Sign-Off Q1/Q2, test-design-epic-4); they are recorded as assumptions, NOT accounting/legally-final. STOP (needs-human) if accounting requires DOCUMENT-LEVEL VAT rounding or a different VAT display / customer-facing VAT wording.

policy.vatRounding: per-line (round each line's VAT, then SUM the rounded line VAT values)
policy.grossDerivation: grossOre = netOre + vatOre (derived; net + VAT are the immutable source of truth)
policy.displayModes: excl / incl / both are presentation-only views over the same net + VAT ore; a mode round-trip returns identical stored ore
policy.privateCustomerInvariant: private customer -> always incl-VAT (gross), not togglable — CONSERVATIVE ASSUMPTION, Sign-Off Q2

lineVatCases.note: Standard Swedish VAT 25% expressed as 2500 bp. net 85000 ore (850,00 kr) -> VAT round(85000*2500/10000)=round(21250)=21250 ore; gross 106250. Exact, no rounding residue.
Reduced Swedish VAT 12% = 1200 bp. net 33300 ore -> VAT round(33300*1200/10000)=round(3996)=3996 ore; gross 37296.
Reduced Swedish VAT 6% = 600 bp. net 50000 ore -> VAT round(50000*600/10000)=round(3000)=3000 ore; gross 53000.
VAT-exempt / 0% = 0 bp. net 85000 ore -> VAT 0 ore; gross 85000. Zero-rate is NOT a special-case bug: the same formula yields 0 cleanly.
Zero-net line at 25% -> VAT 0, gross 0. A zero net row is valid and yields all-zero, not a rejection.

net 2 ore @ 2500 bp -> 2*2500/10000 = 0.5 ore exactly -> round-half-away-from-zero -> 1 (banker's/half-to-even would give 0). Pins the SAME half-mode Story 4.1 golden-pinned into the VAT path; a mode flip here fails loud. gross 3.
net 1 ore @ 2500 bp -> 0.25 ore -> rounds DOWN to 0 (below the .5 boundary) under either mode. Guards the general round-to-nearest path on the VAT computation. gross 1.
net 12345 ore @ 2500 bp -> 3086.25 ore -> rounds to 3086 (residue < .5). Confirms per-line VAT rounding on a non-round net. gross 15431.

fractionalQuantityChainCase.note: Full chain: quantity 2.5 x unitPriceOre 333 -> lineNetOre = roundToOre(832.5) = 833 (Story 4.1 lineNetOre, half-away-from-zero); then VAT @ 2500 bp = roundToOre(833*2500/10000)=roundToOre(208.25)=208; gross 1041. Exercises the fractional-qty -> line-net -> VAT chain end-to-end so a wrong stage fails loud.

sectionTotalCase.note: A section of three lines at DIFFERENT rates: (net 85000 @2500 -> VAT 21250), (net 33300 @1200 -> VAT 3996), (net 50000 @600 -> VAT 3000). Section VAT total = SUM of the already-rounded per-line VAT = 21250+3996+3000 = 28246 (sumOre, sum-of-rounded). Section net = 168300; section gross = sum of per-line gross = 196546.

sumOfRoundedVsRoundOfSumCase.note: LOAD-BEARING divergence pin (R-403). Three identical lines of net 2 ore @ 2500 bp. Per-line VAT = round(0.5) = 1 each -> sum-of-rounded VAT = 1*3 = 3. Round-of-summed-VAT would be round((2+2+2)*2500/10000) = round(1.5) = 2. The engine MUST yield 3 (sum-of-rounded). This diverges from any naive round-at-end implementation (and from Lovable's implicit behaviour) exactly where the conservative pilot policy says it should — hence origin `documented-delta`.
